entities.summary: Gaius Anicius Cerialis was a Roman senator who played a pivotal role in the Principate of the late 1st century CE. Born into a prominent family, he rose through the ranks of Roman politics, becoming suffect consul in 65 CE as the colleague of Gaius Pomponius Pius. This marked a significant moment in the history of the Roman Empire, as it highlighted the increasing power of the imperial office and the struggle for influence among Roman senators. Cerialis's career is notable for its blend of ambition, pragmatism, and loyalty, which ultimately contributed to his success in the complex web of Roman politics. The legacy of Gaius Anicius Cerialis extends beyond his own lifetime, influencing the development of Roman politics and the rise of the Roman Empire as a global power. His contributions to the Principate are still studied by historians today, offering valuable insights into the machinations of Roman politics and the evolution of the Roman state.
